races.name: Download The Tote App Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Andaman Fifty
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Palace Pier filly with strong bloodlines but unknown running style creates tactical uncertainty on debut
runners_data.comment: Palace Pier filly cost 90,000euros as a yearling; top yard, demands plenty of respect
runners_data.spotlight: Palace Pier filly cost 90,000euros as a yearling; half-sister to Listed-placed 1m 2yo winner Defiance (RPR 105); dam placed 7f/1m (76), half-sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Magic Artist, out of half-sister to St Leger and Italian Derby winner Mastery; top yard, newcomer demands plenty of respect.

runners_data.name: Land Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner returning after 235 days with history of fading in finish, making fitness a key concern
runners_data.comment: Plum last on both 2yo starts and easily passed over on seasonal return
runners_data.spotlight: Plum last on both 2yo starts and easily passed over on seasonal return.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fading tendencies running off just 8 days, hard to recommend after disappointing Limerick effort
runners_data.comment: Always behind after slow start on recent Limerick debut; best watched for now
runners_data.spotlight: New Bay filly was a E38,000 yearling; half-sister to 1m4f winner Cycladic (RPR 99); dam 1m2f/1m4f winner (101); always behind after slow start on recent Limerick debut; best watched for now.

runners_data.name: Baiana
runners_data.note: Prominent racer showing much improved form, trainer Joseph O'Brien hitting 20% strike rate, finished ahead of Jackie Jump Up previously
runners_data.comment: Navan second augurs well; contender if handling better ground
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; 100,000euros yearling; dam unraced half-sister to useful German 6f-7f winner Blueridge Silver, out of South African 1m Grade 1 winner; much improved on second outing last October, speed throughout when beaten 0.5l in Navan auction maiden over this trip (Jackie Jump Up a tenderly-ridden neck away third); can go well if handling better ground.

runners_data.name: Aughlish
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse moving from all-weather to turf with solid recent form, the trip return to 6.5f looks ideal after struggling over 6f
runners_data.comment: Ability in AW maidens of late; more likely required on turf debut with cheekpieces tried
runners_data.spotlight: Useful level of form on latest two of three AW starts, showing plenty of pace when close third over 6f and looked in need of a return to this trip when staying-on second to a clear winner over 5f 10 days ago (from a wide draw); cheekpieces now fitted, and likely more required here on turf debut.

runners_data.name: Jackie Jump Up
runners_data.note: Prominent runner seeking revenge on Baiana after narrow defeat at Navan, 193-day break creates fitness question
runners_data.comment: Tenderly-ridden neck off Baiana at Navan; yard have begun the season in fine form
runners_data.spotlight: Much the better of three late-season 2yo outings on final occasion when strong-finishing third (neck off runner-up Baiana) in Navan auction maiden in first-time hood, prompting running and riding enquiry; yard have begun the season in fine form, should go well.

runners_data.name: Glen And Tonic
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with busy campaign experience, recent Curragh run suggests well-being, soft going form gives confidence
runners_data.comment: Curragh comeback run promising but more needed to play a major role here
runners_data.spotlight: Busy 2yo campaign, placed a couple of times on Dundalk AW; at least as good form on last month's seasonal return at the Curragh when beaten under 5l on soft; more needed to play a major role here.

runners_data.name: Star Reign
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fading tendencies and modest form figures, 32 days since last run, hard to recommend at this level
runners_data.comment: Well held in both handicaps this term and hard to see her having an impact back in maiden
runners_data.spotlight: Some promise in 5f turf maidens for Gordon Elliot at the outset of her career; well held in both handicaps this term, and hard to see her having an impact back in maiden company.

races.paceDynamic: Land Of Spirit provides the only confirmed front-running presence but carries concerns about fading in the finish after a 235-day break. This creates a moderate early pace with Baiana, Jackie Jump Up likely to press from prominent positions. The relatively small field and lack of aggressive early speed suggests the pace will be sustainable rather than cut-throat. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and strong finishers who can position themselves to strike in the final two furlongs, with hold-up horses getting the best tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of Spirit sets modest fractions without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too slow for the prominent runners to maintain their kick, allowing the hold-up horses to unleash finishing bursts. Aughlish and Glen And Tonic can time their runs perfectly from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Baiana and Jackie Jump Up press Land Of Spirit creating honest gallop
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and sets up perfectly for horses with tactical speed who can position close enough. Jackie Jump Up gets revenge on Baiana from their previous Navan clash.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of Spirit finds improved fitness and gets easy lead with soft splits
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows the leader to control completely and kick clear when challenged. Baiana becomes the main threat tracking the winner home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Andaman Fifty shows natural ability on debut with Palace Pier bloodlines
scenarios.body: The well-bred filly overcomes inexperience with raw talent, benefiting from the pace scenario to deliver a taking performance. Glen And Tonic provides the main danger from experience.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Land Of Spirit gets an uncontested lead as the 235-day absence could be negated by easy fractions
Monitor Jackie Jump Up's early positioning as any prominent move could create the honest gallop needed for her finishing kick
Check Andaman Fifty's market support as Palace Pier progeny often show ability first time, particularly fillies from this yard
Observe Baiana's tactical placement as she needs to avoid getting caught wide tracking the pace given her prominent style
Watch Glen And Tonic's settling as any keen early racing would compromise his hold-up tactics on this tactical track

races.name: Tote.ie Median Auction Maiden

runners_data.name: Classical Symphony
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suits expected strong pace but concerning form shows consistent fading in finishes
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced 4yo has shown nothing in three starts
runners_data.spotlight: Very lightly-raced 4yo has shown nothing in three starts.

runners_data.name: Little Roy
runners_data.note: Unraced Galileo Gold gelding with promising pedigree but yard struggles with flat maiden winners making debut risky
runners_data.comment: Newcomer likely best watched.
runners_data.spotlight: Galileo Gold gelding; unraced dam closely related to US 1m Grade 2 winner Ryehill Dreamer; yard not known for Flat maiden winners; watch.

runners_data.name: In The Gloaming
runners_data.note: Front-runner will clash with other pace-setters, creating perfect storm for his own defeat despite recent pace-forcing experience
runners_data.comment: Didn't get home on soft at Gowran; probably more one for handicaps in due course
runners_data.spotlight: 33,000euros yearling; half-brother to two winners (5f to 6f, inc Group-placed); last of 12 on debut at the Curragh in September and forced much of pace on seasonal return before fading on soft ground at Gowran last month; probably more one for handicaps in due course.

runners_data.name: Gia Mor
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 324 days with proven good ground form and hold-up style ideal for expected pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Some promise much better-class 2yo maidens early last season; don't rule out on return
runners_data.spotlight: Two juvenile runs came in good-quality maidens in first half of season on good ground, not discredited at both the Curragh and Cork; this looks a much weaker maiden so could be interesting if forward enough.

runners_data.name: County Carlow
runners_data.note: Lead style but highest-rated runner with class edge, though faces immediate pace pressure from two other front-runners
runners_data.comment: Didn't get home over 1m latest; cheekpieces now fitted and marked drop in trip
runners_data.spotlight: 170,000gns yearling; favourite, plenty green when runner-up on debut in Dundalk maiden in late March (7f), following month at same venue forced pace (unbalanced 2f out) but didn't get home over a mile; cheekpieces now fitted and marked drop in trip.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from powerful O'Brien yard returning after 223 days with good ground form and tactical positioning advantage
runners_data.comment: Back in trip for seasonal return and don't rule out
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to useful 6f/7f winners Ejtilaab and Eqtiraan (Listed); okay Curragh debut last summer behind a stablemate but didn't improve as expected at Listowel, finding stamina test (1m, heavy) beyond him; back in trip for seasonal return and don't rule out.

runners_data.name: Keogie
runners_data.note: Front-runner likely to get involved in early pace battle which could compromise his finishing effort despite recent promise
runners_data.comment: Didn't stay 1m latest, previous Curragh second gives him a definite chance
runners_data.spotlight: 21,000euros yearling; half-brother to Czech 7f 2yo/1m3f winner Riwetta; promising Curragh debut in March when staying-on second (4.5l ahead of third-placed Fate's Gambit) over this trip (heavy); didn't get home over a mile under forcing tactics at Gowran last month; return to this trip to suit, and could go well if handling better ground.

runners_data.name: Basilano
runners_data.note: Lead style but lowest-rated runner with consistent poor form making him vulnerable against stronger pace-setters
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last in maidens at the Curragh and Dundalk
runners_data.spotlight: Well-beaten last in maidens at the Curragh and Dundalk.

runners_data.name: Fate's Gambit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form decline could reverse if positioned behind the expected pace battle
runners_data.comment: Return to better ground should suit and this doesn't look a strong maiden
runners_data.spotlight: Went close on debut at Dundalk (7f) in January but hasn't reproduced that level of form in three runs since, not getting home on soft/heavy the last twice at the Curragh and Cork; return to better ground should suit and this doesn't look a strong maiden.

races.paceDynamic: In The Gloaming, County Carlow, and Keogie form a trio of confirmed front-runners who will clash for the early lead over this 6½f trip, creating a fierce gallop from the off. County Carlow showed notable pace-forcing tendencies at Dundalk, while both In The Gloaming and Keogie have displayed similar early speed in recent outings. This sustained battle up front will stretch the field and test stamina reserves in the final furlong. The strong early pace clearly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers with finishing kicks, as the pace-setters will compromise each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners (In The Gloaming, County Carlow, Keogie) engage in sustained battle
scenarios.body: The early leaders will weaken dramatically in the final furlong after their pace war. Classical Symphony and Gia Mor can sweep past with their hold-up style perfectly suited to this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: County Carlow Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If County Carlow can establish a clear lead without maximum pressure
scenarios.body: The 170,000gns yearling can utilize his class edge and controlled pace to hold off late challenges. His runner-up debut form gives him the quality edge in this weaker maiden.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Gia Mor Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the good ground and long absence combine positively for the Murtagh runner
scenarios.body: Gia Mor's hold-up style becomes the perfect weapon after 324 days off, sweeping past tired pace-setters. His previous good ground form at Curragh and Cork shows he has the class for this easier assignment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Substance/Fate's Gambit Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can position perfectly behind the pace battle
scenarios.body: Either Substance or Fate's Gambit could benefit from the O'Brien stable polish or tactical improvement respectively. Their mid-pack positioning allows them to strike when the leaders falter without being too far back.

watchPoints.text: County Carlow and In The Gloaming immediately clash for the lead as both showed clear pace-forcing tendencies in recent runs
Classical Symphony's market support despite poor form could indicate stable confidence in his hold-up style suiting this pace setup
Gia Mor's 324-day absence combined with good ground conditions may produce significant improvement from his hold-up position
Little Roy's debut performance will reveal if the Galileo Gold breeding can overcome yard's poor flat maiden record
The three confirmed front-runners create rare scenario where hold-up horses gain clear tactical advantage from flag-fall

races.name: Tote Never Beaten By SP Handicap

runners_data.name: Polar Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid Navan form but three years without a win creates stamina questions over this extended 6½f trip
runners_data.comment: Likely to be strong at the finish, but the break will be crucial from gate one.
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't won for three years and only had two outings last term; fair fourth in race featuring several of these at Navan  (6f) in March and kept on well from long way back (missed break) when third over 5f there last weekend; likely to be strong at the finish, but the break will be crucial from gate one.

runners_data.name: Rough Diamond
runners_data.note: Former smart handicapper now operating at much lower level, hold-up style suits but form decline is concerning
runners_data.comment: Operating at much lower level now but not showing much for latest trainer; blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Smart handicapper back in the day for Eddie Lynam; wasn't able to add to his tally of five wins when moving to Britain; operating at much lower level nowadays, but not showing much for present trainer who tries blinkers here.

runners_data.name: El Fontenaro
runners_data.note: Maiden whose best form comes at 5f, this trip extension after 198-day break poses stamina concerns despite headgear switch
runners_data.comment: Maiden's best form has been at 5f, including when close third on seasonal debut last term
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden's best form has been at 5f, including on seasonal debut last term when close third at Down Royal; this trip might just stretch her; blinkers swapped for cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Skillman Ave
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with fading tendencies gets 3lb claim but form has nosedived since yard switch from Cromwell
runners_data.comment: Won over 5f last summer; out of form, but few quid for him at Navan and shaped better
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 5f at Tipperary and second over 6f at Fairyhouse last summer when with Gavin Cromwell; very little so far for this yard and mark in freefall; few quid for him at Navan last weekend where he didn't shape too badly.

runners_data.name: Gegenpressing
runners_data.note: Three-time Sligo winner going for hat-trick in this race, hold-up style perfectly suited to expected pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Unbeaten in three runs at Sligo and going for three-in-a-row in this race; nice comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Unbeaten in three runs at Sligo and going for three-in-a-row in this race, the last two coming from stall 16; Hayes is elsewhere today, but quite the substitute to have in the saddle and his comeback run was fine.

runners_data.name: Bel Espoir
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden with fading tendencies has shown nothing in four starts, hard to recommend despite 7lb claim
runners_data.comment: Half-sister to yard's 5f winner Nouvel Espoir, but she hasn't anything yet in four starts
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to yard's 5f winner Nouvel Espoir, but she hasn't anything yet in four starts.

runners_data.name: Ukiyo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid Navan second behind several of these, form gives her leading claims in this company
runners_data.comment: Winner over 6f; had several of these behind when quietly-fancied second at Navan in March
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 6f at Cork on yielding for Gavin Cromwell last year and had several of these behind when quietly-fancied second at Navan in March; decent chance if she's as good around a turning track.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Eagles
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare hasn't won for three years but showed some promise at Down Royal, lacks recent form though
runners_data.comment: Twice second at Down Royal last year after finishing fourth in this; lacks a recent run
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win came over 5f at Down Royal three years ago, but she was twice second at that track last year after finishing fourth (missed break) in this; lacks a recent run this time around.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: Strong-travelling hold-up horse who went close at Navan behind Ukiyo, form suggests he can reverse that result
runners_data.comment: Strong-travelling maiden has run well both starts this season, but can finish tamely
runners_data.spotlight: Strong-travelling maiden went close in 19-runner handicap over 6f at Navan in the autumn, and returned with good effort there in March when just behind Ukiyo (and in front of Polar Bear and Gegenpressing); again found little when let down at Bellewstown latest and head carriage not endearing; might prefer it softer too.

runners_data.name: Star Allure
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden was third in 5f events last year, course fourth gives her some confidence but AW runs were poor
runners_data.comment: Modest performer was third in a couple of 5f maidens last year after C&D fourth in August
runners_data.spotlight: Modest performer was third in a couple of 5f maidens last year after finishing fourth (led) over C&D in August; well held in two AW runs in early 2026.

runners_data.name: March To The Band
runners_data.note: Only prominent racer with fading tendencies, just second turf start but gets to dictate terms up front
runners_data.comment: Yet to place in eight starts and no real progression on AW over the winter
runners_data.spotlight: Back with yard after a spell in Britain; yet to place in eight starts and no real progression on AW over the winter; just second run on turf here.

runners_data.name: Carrickfinn
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with fading tendencies nearly landed gamble at Gowran, money on return suggests stable confidence
runners_data.comment: Modest maiden, but nearly landed a gamble over 1m at Gowran last year and good jockey up
runners_data.spotlight: Donegal-trained prominent racer is modest maiden, but nearly landed a gamble over 1m at Gowran last summer and good effort on AW after; money for him on return when missed break, and jockey booking looks significant.

runners_data.name: Rattletheonionbag
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong Dundalk placed form but turf record is notably inferior to AW performances
runners_data.comment: Lots of placed form on AW, including close third latest, but her turf form isn't as good
runners_data.spotlight: Lots of placed form on AW at Dundalk, including when beaten only half-a-length last month, but still a maiden and her turf form isn't as good.

runners_data.name: My Kurkum
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with fading tendencies was surprise second in this race last year but form fell away afterwards
runners_data.comment: Last year's second in this came out of the blue, also second next time; lost form since
runners_data.spotlight: Seasonal debut second in this race last year came from out of the blue, but he followed it up with another second at Roscommon before losing his form again; no show in two runs this year (excuse last time); different headgear tried.

races.paceDynamic: March To The Band is the lone confirmed pace-setter with prominent tendencies, but his tendency to fade in the finish means he's unlikely to sustain pressure throughout. With most of the field preferring hold-up tactics (Polar Bear, Rough Diamond, El Fontenaro, Gegenpressing, Ukiyo, Happy Henry), the early gallop should be manageable and controlled. The lack of genuine speed horses creates a tactical affair where position into the straight becomes crucial. This moderate pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish, particularly those with proven course form like Gegenpressing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Finish
scenarios.trigger: If March To The Band sets uncontested fractions and the field bunches turning in
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows hold-up horses to get into perfect striking position, creating a sprint finish where class and course knowledge proves decisive. Gegenpressing's three-time Sligo winner status and Ukiyo's solid Navan form behind similar opposition make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If March To The Band stops quickly in the straight and creates a muddling pace throughout
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop becomes pedestrian, turning into a messy sprint where horses with any tactical speed can capitalise on the lack of rhythm. Prominent racers like Skillman Ave and those who can quicken from midfield positions gain the advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Traveller Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays honest and one of the hold-up horses gets a dream run through
scenarios.body: Happy Henry's strong-travelling style allows him to exploit gaps when others are still winding up for their efforts. His recent Navan form behind Ukiyo suggests he's ready to reverse that form with better positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front End Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If March To The Band finds improvement and actually stays the trip under reduced pressure
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to dictate terms and potentially find the stamina that's been missing in recent efforts. His return to turf after AW winter could spark revival.

watchPoints.text: March To The Band's ability to sustain gallop beyond halfway will determine if this becomes tactical or truly-run
Gegenpressing drawn in stall 16 again where he won his last two Sligo victories, but regular rider Hayes is absent
Happy Henry's early positioning will be crucial given his strong-travelling style needs cover in a slowly-run race
Skillman Ave's 3lb claimer Siobhan Rutledge may struggle with pace judgement if this becomes stop-start tactical affair
Money for Carrickfinn on return suggests stable expects improvement from his modest recent AW efforts

races.name: Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid course form who benefits from the likely controlled pace, returning from hurdles spin after 193-day break
runners_data.comment: Had four seconds (three for this rider) and a win last year and this trip suits
runners_data.spotlight: Decent performer over this kind of trip; had four seconds (three for this rider) and a win last year and he's had a spin over hurdles to warm up; ground doesn't matter to him and should be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Circus Act
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with dual-purpose form who can utilise forward position, though maiden on Flat despite hurdles success
runners_data.comment: Fourth to You Make Me Smile in last year's renewal and has nice pull at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Second runner for James Nash; dual-purpose mare has won twice over hurdles; maiden in this sphere but her fourth to You Make Me Smile in last year's renewal was one of her best Flat runs and she has a nice pull at the weights; place chance.

runners_data.name: Pons Aelius
runners_data.note: Forward-going type from improving yard but hasn't been finishing races recently, 107 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Six-time winner at up to 2m in Britain but hasn't shown much for Donegal yard
runners_data.spotlight: Donegal yard likes to pick up horses with back-form, often from Britain, and try to rejuvenate them; six-time winner at up to 2m but hasn't been finishing out his races in Ireland and been off a while.

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: Front-running veteran at 12 years old who may struggle with pace-setting duties if challenging Awakening early
runners_data.comment: Old boy has won 12 races in all under both codes, but pushing on now and looks opposable
runners_data.spotlight: Old boy has won 12 races in all under both codes, mostly from the front; C&D winner in 2024 and was placed over 1m4f last year, but he's pushing on now and tailed off over fences last time.

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from AW success, suits the likely steady tempo but 10-year-old legs are a concern
runners_data.comment: Won over 2m on AW in March; goes well at Ballinrobe and this track isn't dissimilar
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran has done a bit of everything and recorded his eighth win when scoring over 2m on AW in March; poor run at Bellewstown last time but that was only a day after being placed at Dundalk; goes well at Ballinrobe and this track isn't dissimilar.

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: Late-running type who fades in finishes, needs strong pace but may struggle if tempo is too controlled
runners_data.comment: All six wins have come on AW at Dundalk, but went close at Roscommon this time last year
runners_data.spotlight: Not long with Donegal yard and Donegal rider aboard; all six wins have come on AW at Dundalk, but he went close at Roscommon this time last year; best at 1m4f but has run some decent races over 2m.

runners_data.name: Hobart
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trying first-time headgear, limited Flat experience but showed ability in maidens last season
runners_data.comment: Fair hurdler hasn't had much Flat racing and ordinary form on the level thus far; headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Fair hurdler and ran well in a couple of maidens last summer; hasn't had much Flat racing and ordinary form on the level thus far; first time in headgear.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on handicap debut, showed promise over shorter trips and benefits from patient tactics
runners_data.comment: Maiden but plenty of decent efforts over shorter trips; fifth over 1m4f latest; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Third reserve; maiden but plenty of decent efforts over shorter trips last year and, following good run over hurdles, was fifth over 1m4f last weekend; first try at this trip.

runners_data.name: Lisnadill
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with placed form who needs the race run to suit, first run for new stable after 34-day break
runners_data.comment: Narrow defeat when favourite at Naas (10.5f) for previous yard; markedly up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Was placed twice for Andy Oliver last summer, including a narrow defeat when favourite at Naas (10.5f); after a long layoff, finished in rear on stable debut in March; markedly up in trip with new headgear combination tried.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Patient performer who won this race last year, thrives under controlled tempo with strong finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Won this last year and promising run at Navan lately; crack apprentice on board
runners_data.spotlight: Locally-owned mare took a long time to come to hand but thrived under both codes last year, recording four wins including this race and a handicap hurdle here in October; promising run at Navan lately and headgear worn for latest Flat win is back on; crack apprentice on board too, so loads to like.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who switched to hurdles successfully but returning to Flat after 910-day absence
runners_data.comment: Won three hurdles here last year and could be very well handicapped on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Mayo contender was a revelation for his new trainer last year; won three hurdles on decent ground here, latest over 3m1f; showed nothing in Flat maidens as a youngster, but he's a different model nowadays and could be very well in; has won off similar layoff.

runners_data.name: Haughty
runners_data.note: Forward-going type better over shorter trips, 186-day layoff and distance looks beyond optimal range
runners_data.comment: Best form over 7f/1m, stable debut after layoff and not bred for this sort of test.
runners_data.spotlight: Best form over 7f/1m, including sole win in Britain as 3yo; stable debut after layoff and not bred for this sort of test.

runners_data.name: Awakening
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter with modest recent form but tactical advantage of uncontested lead over staying trip
runners_data.comment: With the exception of a decent debut effort, her maiden form has been moderate; tongue-tie
runners_data.spotlight: With the exception of a decent effort on debut, her maiden form has been moderate; not seen since a couple of spins over hurdles last August; tongue-tie on for handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Just For Yuse
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with limited recent Flat racing, returning dual-purpose type who needs patient ride
runners_data.comment: Modest dual-purpose performer has done little Flat racing of late; fair chase run lately
runners_data.spotlight: Modest dual-purpose performer has done little Flat racing of late; returned from nearly two years off in October and ran well when fourth in long-distance chase last month, but easy to look elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Share The Treasure
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needing first run of year, won over this distance but 188-day break is concern
runners_data.comment: Got a win on the board over 1m6f at Navan in August but well held after; may need the run
runners_data.spotlight: Got a win on the board over 1m6f at Navan in August but well held afterwards, and is probably going to need this first run of the year.

runners_data.name: Idomything
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in finishes, beat You Make Me Smile previously but needs strong tempo
runners_data.comment: Beat  You Make Me Smile when winning at Bellewstown in October; well held lately; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: First reserve; got the better of You Make Me Smile when winning at Bellewstown in October but well behind that rival on recent seasonal debut.

races.paceDynamic: Awakening is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field, meaning she'll face no early pressure and can dictate a sustainable tempo through the early stages. The prominent racers Circus Act, Pons Aelius, Hobart and Itsalonglongroad will track behind in the second rank, but none are aggressive pace-pressers. With most of the field comprising hold-up horses including You Make Me Smile, Maxwell Smart, Desert Friend and Autocrat, the pace will be modest early before building gradually. This controlled tempo strongly favours prominent racers and patient hold-up horses who can produce sustained finishes, while making life difficult for any horse needing a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Holders
scenarios.trigger: If Awakening sets uncontested fractions and the pace builds gradually from halfway
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get ideal conditions to unleash finishing kicks, while the modest early tempo ensures stamina reserves remain intact for the final surge. You Make Me Smile and Maxwell Smart can reproduce their best form under these tactical conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the second-rank prominent horses position perfectly and kick before the hold-up brigade
scenarios.body: Circus Act and Hobart can utilise their forward positions to strike in the straight before the back-markers get organised. Their closer proximity to the pace gives them first run on the leaders when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Awakening Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested leader maintains enough in reserve despite setting her own fractions
scenarios.body: The front-runner capitalises on the lack of pace pressure to save energy for a sustained finish, holding off late challengers who leave their runs too late. Her tactical advantage proves decisive over this staying trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Awakening goes too slow early and the race becomes a sprint finish from the back
scenarios.body: The strongest finishers from the rear of the field benefit from an excessively dawdling tempo that turns the race into a dash. Late runners with proven turn of foot can swoop past tiring leaders.

races.paceDynamic: Electric Beauty and Thrifty Of Digby will set the gallop from the gates, with four prominent racers (Yulia, Inthesmallhours, Lady Mairen, Beauparc) creating congestion just behind the leaders through the first half-mile. The honest tempo should suit the patient types initially, but the prominent brigade will apply pressure turning for home as they fan out seeking racing room. This pace setup strongly favours hold-up horses like God Knows and Narlita who can avoid the early scrimmaging and finish fastest when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack creates traffic problems and the early pace proves honest enough
scenarios.body: The patient runners avoid trouble and deliver their finishing kicks when the pace collapses in the final two furlongs. God Knows and Narlita benefit most from their tactical positioning and superior late pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Beauty and Thrifty Of Digby get soft fractions and kick clear turning in
scenarios.body: The leaders exploit the tactical congestion behind them to steal decisive margins before the closers can respond. Electric Beauty's recent fitness edge and Thrifty Of Digby's claiming allowance prove crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactics Win
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers finds a clear passage while others get hampered
scenarios.body: The winner threads through gaps while rivals suffer interference, capitalizing on ideal positioning just behind the pace. Yulia's class or Lady Mairen's connections deliver the goods.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably fast with multiple speed horses engaging
scenarios.body: The race falls apart completely in the final furlong as exhausted leaders surrender to any horse with energy left. So Must I's 3yo allowance or an unconsidered outsider capitalizes.

races.paceDynamic: She's Ideal will likely lead from the off with minimal early pressure, given most of this field are hold-up horses or prefer to come from behind. Spirit Of Indalo and the prominent runners Sarangpur, Copper Craft, Serengeti Sunrise may track the leader but none are confirmed pace-pressers. The majority including Giselles Defence, Keilah, Metamorpheus, Think About It, Cuckaloo Hill, and Angel Harry will settle towards the back expecting the pace to come back to them. This creates a moderate gallop that will quicken late, clearly favouring the hold-up horses who can produce their best work in the final two furlongs when the race truly begins.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady as expected with She's Ideal controlling from the front
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole where the back-markers get first run on tiring leaders. Hold-up specialists with tactical speed will have every chance to strike late when it matters most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal gets an uncontested lead and the hold-up horses leave it too late to challenge
scenarios.body: The leader kicks clear approaching the final furlong while the pack is still getting organized behind. Prominent racers who can sustain their effort will pick up the pieces from those coming too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is particularly sedate and multiple hold-up horses get the same idea simultaneously
scenarios.body: A wall of horses hits the front together in a messy finish where the best stayer prevails. The horse with the strongest late kick from the biggest field of finishers will edge it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the supposed hold-up horses is ridden more aggressively to track the early pace
scenarios.body: This creates better positioning for a horse whose style doesn't typically suit, allowing them to quicken when others are still making ground. The tactically-ridden runner gets first jump on the field.

races.paceDynamic: Misty Cove will take them along at a steady gallop with limited early pressure, while Dawson Street and Nephin Mountain may track prominently but neither is aggressive enough to force a strong pace. The middle section will be comfortable with most of this field sitting back in hold-up positions, creating a bunched field entering the straight. This moderate early tempo over 1m2½f will set up a sprint finish where those with tactical speed and finishing kick will have the advantage. The race shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can produce their best effort late rather than those needing to be prominent throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate throughout and creates a sprint finish from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The patient tactics suit the majority who prefer to be delivered late, with superior finishing speed deciding the outcome rather than stamina. Those held up can pick off the early leaders who face the longest sustained effort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Misty Cove and Nephin Mountain can dictate ideal fractions without being headed too early
scenarios.body: Their forward positions avoid the scrimmaging behind and they can use superior fitness or tactical awareness to hold off late challengers. The pace becomes honest enough to test the finishing kicks of those held up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If several horses move forward simultaneously approaching the home turn, forcing the tempo
scenarios.body: This creates a more searching test that plays to those with genuine stamina rather than pure finishing speed. The sustained gallop from 4f out finds out those dependent on a final flourish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Apprentice Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the inexperienced riders find better positions or get cleaner runs than the senior jockeys
scenarios.body: Their mounts avoid interference while more fancied runners get caught in traffic or face impossible tasks from poor positions. The weight allowances become crucial in a tight finish.
